title: The Well of the Bell House
premise: Dominic Dunmore, a rationalist hospice nurse, takes a temporary post in the village of Bell House, where the dying all count backwards from nineteen and speak of a bell that was melted down in 1911. When the phantom bell rings on his first night, Dominic begins hearing it too—and realizes the backwards counting is a summons, not a symptom. The village founders left an unfinished ritual that must be completed before the harvest moon or the bell will ring in everyone who ever died there. In the end, Dominic discovers he is descended from the founder who broke the ritual, and by ringing the recast bell himself—choosing truth over belonging—he frees the village but loses his place in it.
about_author: Odile Zhou is a former palliative care volunteer who writes horror about the quiet bargains people make with belief. She lives near the coast, where she collects church bells the way other people collect regrets.

chapters.title: Nineteen
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. On his last shift at the hospice, a dying woman counts backwards from nineteen and dies exactly at zero. Dominic documents it as coincidence, but his hands shake. Emotional beat: the first crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: The Village That Melted Its Bell
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. He arrives in Bell House for a live-in nursing post caring for elderly Ada Voss. The locals are warm but watchful; no one will say why the church tower stands empty. Beat: unease dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Zero at Midnight
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Ada counts backwards in her sleep—nineteen to zero—and at zero, a bell tolls though the tower holds nothing. Dominic searches the tower and finds only scorch marks and a rope worn smooth by hands long dead. Beat: dread arrives without explanation.

chapters.title: What the Dying Know
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. He interviews other villagers' dying relatives; every one of them counts. The vicar, Reverend Hale, warns him gently to stop asking. Beat: the community closes ranks, and Dominic feels both threatened and strangely included.

chapters.title: Ada's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Ada, lucid for the first time in weeks, tells him the founders rang the bell to bind the village's dead to its soil—a mercy, she says, so no one leaves alone. Then she resumes counting. Beat: loyalty and horror entwined.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the parish archive he finds the 1911 ledger: seven founders, six signatures, one line torn out. The melted bell was never fully melted—something was poured into the metal instead. Beat: curiosity becomes compulsion.

chapters.title: First Ringing
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The bell rings at noon before the whole village, and everyone bows their heads except Dominic. A child asks him why he didn't kneel. That night someone nails a sprig of rowan to his door. Beat: belonging offered at a price.

chapters.title: The Sixth Signature
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. He matches the torn ledger line to a name: Dunmore. His own great-grandfather was the seventh founder who fled before the ritual finished. Beat: identity collapses; the story was always about him.

chapters.title: Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Reverend Hale. Hale reveals the village knows what Dominic is: the bloodline that can finish the ritual. Finish it, and the dead rest forever; refuse, and the bell will ring them all up at harvest moon. Beat: temptation framed as duty.

chapters.title: Counting Backwards
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic starts counting in his sleep. He wakes at the window, hand raised toward the tower. The ritual is already working through him whether he consents or not. Beat: loss of bodily sovereignty.

chapters.title: The Melted Man
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A figure of cooling bronze appears at the edge of the churchyard—the founder who stayed, fused into the bell's making, still half-aware. It speaks his family name. Beat: horror made intimate and ancestral.

chapters.title: Rowan and Salt
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Villagers begin protecting him—meals, gifts, vigilance—as if he were already theirs. For the first time in his drifting life, Dominic belongs somewhere. Beat: the seduction of loyalty at its strongest.

chapters.title: Ada Reaches Zero
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Ada dies at zero, smiling, and does not stay dead—she stands at her window each dusk, counting again. Grief curdles into resolve. Beat: the personal cost made flesh.

chapters.title: The Ritual Fragment
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. From Ada's effects he recovers the founders' rite: the bell must be rung by willing blood at harvest moon, or the binding reverses and every bound dead rises. Beat: the stakes crystallize into a deadline.

chapters.title: Doubt in the Belfry
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic finds evidence the 'mercy' was a lie—the founders bound the dead to hide a drowning, a crime the bell has been covering for a century. Beat: loyalty versus truth reaches open war inside him.

chapters.title: They Ask Him to Stay
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The village throws him a harvest feast; Hale publicly names him heir of Bell House. Warmth everywhere, and underneath it, a threat: refuse, and be counted among the dead. Beat: belonging revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: The Bronze Speaks
chapters.summary: POV the bronze figure. The fused founder begs Dominic—not to finish the rite, but to end it, even if it means the dead rise briefly and the village grieves honestly at last. Beat: the moral pivot.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The moon swells red over the empty tower. Half the village gathers to help him complete the ritual; the other half, led by Hale, waits to see which way he breaks. Beat: the eve of decision, tension at maximum.

chapters.title: Ringing
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. At moonrise Dominic climbs the tower, recasts the clapper from the bronze figure's released core, and rings the bell backward—unbinding rather than binding. The dead rise, weep, name their true histories, and fall silent forever. Beat: climax; truth chosen over comfort.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Sound
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The village wakes grieving and free. Some thank him; more turn away. Hale, stripped of purpose, asks why Dominic couldn't just have belonged. Beat: the cost of truth made plain.

chapters.title: The Empty Tower
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic packs to leave. No one counts anymore; the dying simply stop. He visits Ada's grave and finds it marked with rowan—kept, after all, by someone who loved him. Beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: One
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. On the road out, Dominic passes a hospice and stops—there are still people counting somewhere, waiting for someone unafraid to listen. He goes in. Beat: resolution as vocation; the skeptic becomes the keeper of endings.
